title: Victoria Monét Reveals ‘Frequency of Love’ Track List, Featuring Bruno Mars, SZA, Bryson Tiller & Leon Thomas
summary: Frequency of Love arrives on Oct. 2.
body: Victoria Monét’s Frequency of Love album is set to arrive next Friday, Oct. 2, and the Grammy-winning singer just revealed the LP’s star-studded track list. Monét released a trailer for Frequency of Love , which recruits a range of collaborators across R&B, including SZA, Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas, Bryson Tiller, Chlöe and Lucky Daye. VM’s daughter, Hazel, will also make a special guest appearance. Monét unveiled the track list with a cinematic trailer for the album, which saw excited fans claiming their favorite songs in the comments, while peers expressed they were hyped to see what Vic has in store come Oct. 2. “This album is about to be insanityyyyy. grateful to be apart,” Chlöe wrote. title: ‘Gilded Age’ Cast Comes Together for First Holiday Album: Full Track List
summary: Noted producer/songwriter Desmond Child helmed the project, which includes many Tony Award-winning performers.
body: As fans of The Gilded Age know, HBO’s Emmy-nominated series about America’s massive move into industrialization in the late 1800s and the robber barons who drove and profited from the rapid growth, is stacked with Broadway actors in its cast. Now, many of the actors, including Tony winners Brian Stokes Mitchell, Christine Baranski, Kelli O’Hara, Laura Benanti, Donna Murphy and Audra McDonald, will be featured on Voices of the Gilded Age: The Christmas Album , out Nov. 6 on Concord Theatricals Recordings. The release comes days after the season 4 premiere of the show on Nov. 1. Grammy-nominated producer/songwriter Desmond Child conceived and helmed the set, which features classic holiday songs, as well as two original songs, penned by Child. “I’ve been waiting my whole life to make this record, and I’m still in awe that I was able to bring it to life alongside some of Broadway’s most extraordinary voices,” Child said in a statement. “Together we’ve created a loving tribute to our favorite Christmas songs, legendary artists, lyricists, composers, and arrangers whose timeless music has warmed our hearts and filled our lives with joy.” The album expanded on what are widely considered …

summary: Five alternatives entered and only one could top our poll, but there was a bigger surprise at the bottom.
body: The Pixel 11 Pro is objectively a very good phone, but at a cool $1,100, it’s hardly a no-brainer in the current market. Indeed, it has plenty of competition. title: Searching for Googlebooks won’t give you the results you’re looking for
summary: Google is facing some funny SEO irony for ‘Googlebooks’ queries.
body: Credit: Richard Priday / Android Authority TL;DR A new category of laptops, called Googlebooks, was recently launched. The laptops share a very similar name to the company’s index of actual books. When searching for these notebooks on the company’s search engine, the first page of results is for Google Books. This has been a big week for Google, as pre-orders for Googlebooks opened up on Monday. Googlebooks are a new category of laptops that combine ChromeOS and Android into a single desktop operating system, for those unaware. So far, it seems these notebooks are selling like hotcakes, as the laptops are already out of stock on the company’s US store . If you’re interested in learning more about these computers, don’t bother turning to Search, as you won’t find what you’re looking for. As it turns out, Googlebooks have somewhat of an SEO problem. Spotted by The Verge , typing Googlebooks into Google Search will instead get you results for the tech giant’s index of actual books. The company’s digital database for full-text books and magazines just happens to share a very similar name with its new laptops, Google Books. An oversight you’d think the Mountain View-based firm would’ve…

title: John Legend Takes Inspiration From His ‘Ordinary People’ Video for Cinematic ‘Fireflies’ Visual
summary: Fully produced by Pharrell, the Grammy-winning singer's Muse album arrives next month.
body: John Legend and Pharrell have been friends for over two decades, and they’re gearing up for their first collab album with Skateboard P producing the entirety of Legend’s upcoming Muse LP, which will be released on Oct. 23 via Republic Records. The duo teamed up to release the second single from the project as “Fireflies” arrived on Friday (Sept. 25). For the classy music video, Legend hops behind his Yamaha piano to perform the ethereal track with some help from the Hollywood Cinematic Orchestra, who are suited and booted. The seamless white backdrop is reminiscent of the visual from John Legend’s “Ordinary People,” which originally served as a single for his 2004 Get Lifted album. The will.i.am-assisted ballad peaked at No. 24 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won a Grammy for best male vocal R&B performance, while receiving nominations in the song of the year and best R&B song categories. In a similar vein, “Fireflies” finds Legend singing about turning hardship to hope while navigating the turbulence and hurdles life has thrown his way. “Pharrell’s idea from the beginning was that we would create something with all of the…

title: Soft Cell Talks the ‘Zeitgeist’ Coincidence of Releasing a ‘Danceteria’ Song the Same Year as Madonna
summary: Marc Almond reflects on Danceteria, the synth-pop duo’s final album after the loss of his bandmate David Ball.
body: “Bittersweet” is Marc Almond’s term for Danceteria, the sixth and final Soft Cell album which is out Friday (Sept. 25), 11 months after longtime partner David Ball passed away at the age of 66. “It wasn’t a complete surprise, but I thought we still would’ve had more time together to see through this album, at least, and who knows what for the future,” Almond tells Billboard of Ball’s death, which came after years of extensive health issues. “I’d been in contact with him just two days before and we both ticked off the album and said how pleased we are with it, then two days later he passed away. So the album’s finally coming out, and I just wish Dave was around to enjoy it.” Almond, 69, had an early chance to witness how Danceteria would be received on this summer’s Generations Tour with the Human League and Alison Moyet, during which he previewed three of its 14 songs, including the title track and the album-closing remake of Was (Not Was)’s “Out Come the Freaks” recorded with Nona Hendryx. The album was actually a couple of years in the making and originally planned to be released during the sprin…

summary: Z Fold 8 Ultra seems to have it worse than others.
body: TL;DR Users of several Samsung phones are reporting YouTube playback issues. Navigating away from YouTube and back while a video is playing can cause the video to freeze. Case in point: a number of users of the $2,100 Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra have reported that the YouTube app isn’t working correctly on their phones. title: As America Observes Dolly Day, a Look at The Enduring Qualities of ‘9 To 5’
summary: “What this [songwriting] job is, it’s empathy,” says Steve Earle. “A song like ‘9 to 5’ is sort of the ultimate statement of that."
body: Ella Langley set a record with her 23rd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with “Choosin’ Texas,” a song that — because of the fragmentation in modern formats — is still unknown to a fair amount of music fans. Dolly Parton , by contrast, got just two weeks at the top on the pop list in 1981 with “9 to 5,” and just about everyone knew it. Inside and out. Related Today Is Dolly Parton Day – It’s 9/25 Bono Says Dolly Parton ‘Sang Her Heart Out’ for Her Final Recording With U2 Kacey Musgraves to Perform on 2026 VMAs in Tribute to Dolly Parton Forty-five years later, in the wake of Parton’s death on Aug. 25, much of America is celebrating Dolly Day on Sept. 25 — not because it marks one month since her passing, but because Sept. 25 is represented numerically as 9/25. Or “9 to 5.” It may not be recognized as her greatest song, but that’s just because her catalog is so competitive that “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors” or “I Will Always Love You” tend to beat it when analysts consider such things. But when it became the theme song of the movie that first put her on the big screen — alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin — “9 to 5” finished the job that she’d st…

title: Where’s my timestamp? Google Messages is updating its UI, and users are confused
summary: Messages introduces new swipe controls for your chat's metadata.
body: TL;DR Back in 2024, Google first started working on swipe gestures to view timestamps in Messages. That new interface is now widely rolling out to users. Messages also now supports swiping right to directly reply. When you’re looking back on your text message history, it’s not just the texts and the GIFs you care about. The metadata also tells a story, too: when messages were sent, if they went out with encryption, and whether or not they were even received. If you’re opening up Google Messages this week but suddenly are having trouble finding some of those details, worry not — Google’s just tweaking how you access them. So far, when you’ve gone to tap on a message in your chat history, Messages would pull up its metadata right below: timestamp, delivery status, encryption — the works. But 9to5Google has now spotted a new design that’s been rolling out to more and more users, changing up how we see this info — and it’s not without its improvements.

title: Google Calendar is getting an update that global teams will appreciate
summary: Google Calendar is rolling out a big win for distributed teams.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Users can now configure Google Calendar to display up to three time zones. You’ll be able to add custom labels to each time zone that’s displayed. This update will be available to Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts. In late August, Google rolled out a much-welcomed feature to the Calendar app. The change gave meeting organizers and their delegates the ability to choose whether or not to receive RSVP emails and automatic responses. This month, Calendar is getting another update that should prove convenient for team members in other time zones. While converting time zones isn’t the hardest thing in the world to do, it is inconvenient. Especially so if your meetings are frequently set to a time zone other than yours. Fortunately, Google is addressing this problem by allowing more time zones to be displayed on Calendar.

title: This Nintendo DS-themed launcher is coming to dual-screen Android handhelds

body: TL;DR An update to the Nintendo DS-themed Nitrodeck Launcher is set to make the launcher compatible with dual-screen Android handhelds. Developer Mr. Rubik has posted a video of the launcher running on the Anbernic RG DS handheld. Mr. Rubik says the update should be available on the Play Store sometime either this week or next. Affordable Android-based gaming handhelds have been gaining in popularity lately, and they come in a wide range of shapes and sizes. A handful have two screens, making them ideal for emulating games that originally appeared on the dual-screen Nintendo DS. This week, the developer of the DS-themed Nitrodeck Launcher announced that an update to make the launcher compatible with these dual-screen devices is coming soon. As brought to our attention by Retrododo , developer Mr. Rubik has been showing off an update for Nitrodeck Launcher that makes it compatible with Android handhelds that come with two screens. He’s also published a video showing the launcher running on the Anbernic RG DS handheld , and the software certainly looks the part.

title: A Google Photos bug is preventing users from sharing, editing, and deleting pictures
summary: Can’t delete or share pictures after editing in Google Photos? You’re not alone.
body: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel owners are experiencing an issue with the Google Photos editor. Options like sharing, deleting, and editing become unresponsive after a photo is edited. The issue appears to be affecting multiple generations of Pixel phones. Google is currently working on powering up editing in the Photos app by improving the markup tools . In case you haven’t seen our previous coverage, we recently found evidence that Google could add a brush size slider, more colors, text alignment, and more. But before those changes are rolled out, the company may want to look into a new problem affecting the app’s editor. After you take a photo, the Google Photos editor lets you perform a variety of actions, which include sharing, editing, deleting, and adding to an album. Normally, you can perform one of these actions and immediately follow that up with another. For example, if you made an edit to a picture, you could also share the image without leaving the editor. However, it appears a bug has broken this functionality.

title: Some Pixel users are locked out after the September 2026 update
summary: Is your pattern or PIN unlock not working after the September 2026 update? You’re not alone.
body: TL;DR A few Pixel users have been unable to get through their lock screen following the September 2026 update. The issue appears to affect users with a pattern lock enabled on the lock screen, though at least one user with a PIN also reported a similar problem. This bug doesn’t appear to be widespread yet, though Google appears to be aware of the problem. The recent September Pixel Drop introduced a revamped Pixel VIPs widget, expanded scam protection to other chat apps through Gboard, and fixed several bugs. However, some have found that not everything is working as expected, with reports of users being unable to access their phones appearing online. According to a Pixel 10 Pro XL owner on Reddit who installed the recent update, the phone refused to recognize the pattern unlock they set up. They reportedly tried booting the phone in safe mode a few times, cleaning the screen, restarting it, and even connecting a mouse with an adapter, but saw no results.

title: ATV Launcher’s latest update brings big home screen upgrades for your Android TV
summary: Version 0.1.41 rolls out custom row layouts, inline widgets, a modular status bar, and refreshed tile designs.
body: TL;DR ATV Launcher v0.1.41 adds “Arrangements,” featuring 10 fixed row layouts, and lets users place widgets directly inside app rows via a tile context menu. The update also includes an upgraded Configure Tile dialog with live previews, new folder preview styles, edge-to-edge Watch Next cards, and a separate free companion app with 15 clock styles. Users also get a fully customizable status bar with floating or fixed placements, toggleable icons, pill styles, and direct TV input switching. If you have ever felt fed up with the ad-heavy, recommendation-bloated interfaces taking over your Android TV-based TVs and streaming sticks and boxes, chances are you’ve explored how to install a Google TV launcher alternative . Among the most iconic tools in that space is ATV Launcher, which received its 0.1.40 update last month, featuring a new layout editor. Now, the developer is keeping that update momentum going with the rollout of ATV Launcher v0.1.41.

title: Pixel 11 signal problems? Try these 7 fixes before returning it
summary: Don't give up on your Pixel 11 before trying these simple fixes.
body: One of the biggest changes Google made with the Pixel 11 series is the switch to a new MediaTek modem. We’ve already seen that moving away from Samsung’s Exynos modem has delivered a noticeable generational improvement over the Pixel 10 series and brought Google’s connectivity much closer to the competition. That said, not every Pixel 11 owner is having a smooth experience. Some users are reporting issues with mobile data and Wi-Fi connectivity on their Pixel 11 phones. While the number of reports appears smaller than what we’ve seen with previous generations, connectivity problems can still be incredibly frustrating.

title: The Galaxy Watch 9 is a great watch with one problem you’ll notice every day
summary: Samsung's latest smartwatch is better, faster, and frustratingly familiar.
body: I’ve been wearing a Galaxy Watch 7 for two years. Samsung threw trade-in offers at me throughout the Watch 8 cycle, and I didn’t bite, partly because I was between jobs at the time and partly because my Watch 7 was still doing everything I needed. So when the Galaxy Watch 9 () showed up, I was ready to be impressed. Two generations is a long time to sit out. Whatever Samsung had been cooking for its new smartwatches , I was going to feel all of it at once. But after three weeks of using it, I’ve realized that while the Galaxy Watch 9 is a very good smartwatch, it’s not one I can wholeheartedly recommend without one very familiar asterisk.

title: Some Pixel owners are still missing alarms because of a years-old Clock bug
summary: Pixels are still sleeping through their own alarms, and so is Google.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Some Pixel owners are still struggling with a long-standing bug that prevents alarms from going off. All they get is a notification that says “alarm didn’t fire for an unknown reason.” The issue has been around since at least 2021, and Google previously promised to fix it, though it seems that’s not the case. Google Pixel phones have a long-standing bug with the Clock app that prevents alarms from going off on time. It has hampered users’ experience for years now, and we can trace reports back to as early as 2021 . While Google claimed to have fixed it, newer reports keep cropping up every now and then, and that hasn’t changed. We’ve spotted newer reports coming from Pixel users about the alarm not firing when intended. According to screenshots shared by users, these missed alarms occur for an “unknown reason.” Mysterious reasons that Google had promised to address, but hasn’t.

title: How to hide your phone’s IMEI number from the lock screen — and why you should
summary: Making your device's IMEI number easy to access comes with some compromises.
body: Google’s been rolling out a setting to many Android devices that can make your phone’s IMEI — a unique, unchangeable number that identifies your individual device — accessible from the lock screen . This can potentially help you recover a lost or stolen device by providing easy proof of ownership, but because there are ways for bad actors to exploit an exposed IMEI, it’s also something of a security risk. Making your device identifier accessible from the lock screen is optional, though. Here’s what you need to know, and how to change the relevant setting on your own phone.

title: F-Droid’s biggest update in a decade is coming despite Google’s sideloading crackdown
summary: F-Droid's latest update goes beyond a redesign, refining search and updates.
body: Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority TL;DR F-Droid is getting its biggest update in a long time, bringing improved visuals and better flows. The team says the app has been rewritten entirely to make it easier to support in the coming years. Besides more modern visuals, F-Droid brings improved search, categories, and a seamless update method. F-Droid, the most popular app store for free and open-source Android apps, is about to get its biggest update in a decade. As one of the biggest critics of Google’s new sideloading restrictions in Android , F-Droid is bracing for the change with a modern interface that makes app discovery feel far less intimidating. In a recent blog post detailing version 2.0 , F-Droid said the new app store experience improves search and offers a “simpler experience that works well.” Visuals definitely feel refreshed, and the app now supports Google’s Material Design for aesthetics that feel more modern and cohesive with the rest of Android. The team says the update goes beyond a visual refresh, and that the app has been rewritten in Kotlin to ensure more frequent updates in the future.

title: This benched Lenovo Googlebook 2-in-1 tablet poses for another high-quality leak

Traditionally, this feature required a specific mechanism to sync gameplay across multiple devices and was therefore limited to scenarios where all players are on the same operating system—and to desktop environments. That changes now with Dolphin announcing NetPlay support for Android and opening it up for cross-platform gameplay. title: Google Messages has a camera flash problem, and nobody knows why

In some cases, the LED flash simply refuses to activate even when toggled manually, though it functions normally in other camera apps. Apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Google Messages , along with several others, offer a camera interface in the chat to capture and send media. title: Data privacy isn’t just for nerds — here’s why you should care too
summary: The more I see how my personal data is used across services, the more I want to guard my privacy.
body: A lot of times when I’ve mentioned moving to more privacy-focused apps and services, the reaction is more than a shrug — it’s a declaration that online privacy isn’t all that important. Most recently, at a tech event, I mentioned moving to Brave to avoid Google’s data collection and targeted advertising, and another attendee said that it’s just not important to them. That’s when I realized that there’s this general misunderstanding that prioritizing data privacy is the pastime of nerds and those prone to donning tin foil hats. I know I was someone who used to take a more laissez-faire approach to my online privacy. Years later, after grappling with the consequences of this, I feel that data privacy and data collection should be something everyone cares about.
